_comment_domain_review: 2026-07-21 domain-accuracy correction (Task 2 review): EUPL-1.0/1.1/1.2 moved from weak-copyleft to strong-copyleft - the EUPL's Art. 5 copyleft clause is whole-work reciprocal (closer to GPL than to MPL's file-level scope), and EUPL-1.2 extends the reciprocity trigger to network 'Communication' (AGPL-like); the FSF treats it as GPL-comparable, not weak/file-level. NGPL moved from permissive to strong-copyleft - despite the permissive-sounding name, its actual text carries a GPL-style whole-work reciprocity clause requiring derivatives to also be NGPL-licensed. Motosoto moved from permissive to weak-copyleft as a deliberate conservative call, not a high-confidence one: Motosoto derives from the Jabber Open Source License (MPL/Netscape-lineage), which carries file-level reciprocity on modifications, so 'permissive' risked a silent NONE result; this follows the same safe-direction pattern already applied to QPL-1.0 (weak-copyleft over permissive, to over-flag to REVIEW rather than risk missing a real conflict). Motosoto is an extremely rare license in practice, so real-world stakes here are low.
